content.comment_body: I'm experiencing fluctuating signal input from a temperature interface board. The type K thermocouple I'm using has a metal shield, but it's not yet connected to any earth. When I touch the shield, the signal reading on the [product_name] changes. Should the shield of the sensor be connected to the protective earth (PE) or functional earth (FE)? ...sent from App

Hi [user_name], you should connect the shield to the FE terminal and also connect the FE terminal to PE. Refer to the attachment for an example—the AM2 module illustration demonstrates how the shield and PE are linked.

analysis.insight_summary: A user is facing unstable signal readings from a temperature interface board with a shielded type K thermocouple on a [product_name] device. The discussion reveals uncertainty about how shielding and grounding should be handled, which points to a broader need for clearer installation instructions for sensor wiring and grounding in automation setups. Responses suggest users want easy-to-follow, well-documented guidance to ensure safe and reliable sensor integration.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for straightforward instructions on wiring—particularly whether to connect the shield to earth—to achieve stable and precise signal readings with their thermocouple and [product_name] system.
